Plot whether subjects are identified by their own earlier sample

Source: R/AllGenerics.R, R/plotFingerprint.R, R/zzz-mae.R
plotFingerprint.Rd

plotFingerprint() compares, for each subject, the sample at a query time with all samples at a reference time. A subject is identified when its own reference sample is closer than the reference sample of any other subject.

Usage

plotFingerprint(x, ...)

# S4 method for class 'SummarizedExperiment'
plotFingerprint(x, dissimilarity, time.col, group, time.point, ...)

# S4 method for class 'MultiAssayExperiment'
plotFingerprint(x, ..., experiment = 1L)

Arguments

x

a SummarizedExperiment object.

...

additional arguments passed to geom_point.

dissimilarity

Character scalar. Specifies the sample by sample dissimilarity in metadata(x), as stored by mia::addDissimilarity().

time.col

Character scalar. Specifies the column from colData(x) that contains sampling times: numeric, Date, POSIXct or a factor of visits.

group

Character scalar. Specifies the column from colData(x) that identifies subjects.

time.point

Vector of two values of time.col: the reference time, whose samples subjects are identified from, and the query time, whose samples are identified.

experiment

Character scalar or integer scalar. For a MultiAssayExperiment, the experiment to plot; its samples get the colData of x. (Default: 1L)

Value

A ggplot object.

Details

Each point is a subject with samples at both times: the dissimilarity of its query sample to its own reference sample (x) and to the nearest reference sample of another subject (y). Points above the 1:1 line are identified. The subtitle gives the share of subjects identified. Franzosa et al. (2015) identified people by metagenomic codes; this plot applies the same idea to the nearest sample on a dissimilarity.

References

Franzosa EA, et al. (2015). Identifying personal microbiomes using metagenomic codes. PNAS 112(22):E2930-E2938.

Examples

# Is each subject's second sample closest to its own first sample?
data("hitchip1006", package = "miaTime")
tse <- hitchip1006
# Some profiles are stored twice; keep the first copy
tse <- tse[, !duplicated(t(SummarizedExperiment::assay(tse, "counts")))]
tse$visit <- factor(ave(tse$time, tse$subject, FUN = rank))
tse <- tse[, tse$visit %in% c("1", "2")]
tse <- mia::addDissimilarity(tse, method = "bray", assay.type = "counts")
plotFingerprint(tse, dissimilarity = "bray", time.col = "visit",
    group = "subject", time.point = c("1", "2"))
#> Warning: 'group' has 929 subjects with a single sample.
